title: Instrumentation sandbox lab notes: exploratory metrics and tracing
content:
Purpose:
This is an exploratory "lab" doc for quick experiments in metric naming, trace anchor placement, and dashboard widgets that support fast incident investigation for tokenized inference. The goal is a small set of lightweight, low-cost signals that answer 80% of common investigations (latency spike, increased cost per token, degraded quality fallback) and play nice with sampling budgets.

Audience and context:
- Audience: SREs, runtime engineers, product reliability PMs, and anyone instrumenting inference pipelines.
- Context: hosted + dedicated deployments. We need metrics that work for multi-tenant and single-tenant scenarios with minimal per-tenant tag explosion.

Quick experiment log (chronological):
- 2024-09-12: Baseline probe added: inference.request.duration_ms (histogram) + trace anchors for request.recv, model.load, kv.cache.hit, decode.start, token.generated.
- 2024-09-18: Small-scale sampling enabled: 100% SLI traces for p95/p99 slow requests; head sampling 1% for adaptive profiling.
- 2024-09-25: Added compact per-route cost tag: billing.unit_estimate (micro-tokens) emitted once per request.
- 2024-09-30: Dashboard prototype with three investigation lanes: Latency, Cost, Error/Quality.
- 2024-10-03: Observed noise in quantization-switch metrics; added model.variant label to reduce ambiguity.

Naming & tag conventions (experiment proposal):
- Metric prefix: inference. (keeps metrics grouped in dashboards and avoids collisions)
- Use snake_case for metric names, dot for hierarchical grouping: inference.request.duration_ms, inference.kv.cache_hit_rate (gauge), inference.decode.tokens_per_sec (gauge), inference.model.load_ms (summary), inference.fallback.count (counter)
- Labels (limited set): env, region, model, model_variant, route, tenant_id_truncated (8 chars), outcome (success|fallback|error|timeout), batching_strategy (none|auto|fixed)
- Keep tenant_id_truncated to avoid high cardinality. If tenant-level drilldown required, use separate logs or high-card correlation sampling.

Traces: anchor design and span strategy
- Minimal span set per request: client.recv -> router.route -> runtime.queue -> worker.exec -> model.decode -> client.send.
- Anchor spans: router.route (route decision), runtime.queue (queue time), worker.exec (gpu time), model.decode (decode loop).
- Add attributes on model.decode spans: sequence_length, kv_cache_used (bool), prefix_cache_hit_count (int).
- Trace ID tagging: emit trace_id and sampling_flag in logs for session join-ups. Avoid full trace logging for 100%; rely on span snapshots for top quantiles.

Sampling experiments and heuristics (notes):
- Budget: target 0.1% full-trace rate cluster-wide for long-term retention; 10% for p99 / slow requests for short window (1h).
- Heuristic sampling triggers: latency > p95, fallback triggered, route flagged as experimental, or explicit manual probe via /debug/trace endpoint.
- Adaptive sampling pilot: start at 0.05% baseline; scale to 5% for traced requests in the calendar minute if cluster error-rate > 2% (to gather more context).

Dashboard prototype (investigation flows):
- Page layout (top to bottom): global health row -> latency heatmap and p50/p95/p99 sparklines -> cost per token panel by model -> trace-linked request table -> route-level mini-profiles -> quick actions (replay, enable debug, tag for w/e rollout).
- Widgets:
  * Latency heatmap: buckets [0-10ms, 10-50ms, 50-200ms, 200-1000ms, >1000ms] broken out by route. Clicking a bucket shows sampled traces.
  * Cost per token: show median and 95th, with model_variant breakdown. Include an estimated $/1M tokens calc in header derived from billing.unit_estimate.
  * Route-level mini-profiles: small stacked bar showing queue time vs exec time vs decode time per route.
  * Trace-linked request table: columns: timestamp, route, tenant_id_truncated, latency_ms, outcome, model_variant, trace_link. Allow quick filter to show only fallback=true.

Investigation play examples (how to use widgets):
- Latency spike on p95: open heatmap -> filter to route with spike -> open trace for a slow example -> check runtime.queue vs worker.exec to see whether congestion or model slow path. If kv_cache_used=false and sequence_length large, consider recommending prefix caching.
- Increased cost: open cost panel -> group by model_variant -> if cost jumps but latency steady, check batch sizes and token_length distribution (decode.tokens_per_sec).

Cost & retention notes (very rough):
- Estimated cardinality impact for model_variant + route: moderate. Traces dominate cost; expect ~10x storage for traces sampled at 1% vs metrics only.
- Short-term plan: keep high-fidelity traces for 7 days at higher sampling for p99, then archive sampled traces for 30d in compressed format. Metrics retention: 90d full-resolution; 365d aggregated.

Open questions & follow-ups:
- How do we surface model-quality regressions (hallucination) in telemetry? Proposed signal: inference.eval.regression_count tied to daily eval prompt set runs; needs product alignment.
- Tenant-level drilldown: do we accept a special high-card route for flagged tenants, or rely on log correlation? Action: decision in next runbook sync (ENGOBS-432).
- Does dedicated capacity routing require different labels (pool_id vs region)? Action: run small experiment adding pool_id label for dedicated-only metrics.

Mini TODO list (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Add outcome label to fallback metrics and emit at the runtime gateway (assigned: Samir)
- [ ] Implement adaptive sampling prototype (assigned: Eleni)
- [ ] Wire up trace_link column in the dashboard to the trace viewer (assigned: Jordan)
- [ ] Run 2-week cost simulation for 1% vs 0.1% trace sampling (assigned: Maya)

Notes to self / scratch fragments:
- consider low-cardinality feature flags for experimental routes instead of tags
- prefer histogram for durations with explicit buckets aligned to SLO boundaries instead of only summaries
- can we piggyback model.variant from model registry instead of runtime string? better TTL on registration

Relevant links / tickets:
- ENGOBS-432 (tenant drilldown decision)
- github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/128 (adaptive sampler prototype)
- confluence:Observability-Lab-Notebook-2024 (larger notebook)

Summary (one-liner):
This doc is a living lab for low-friction telemetry experiments: concise metric names, a small set of anchor spans, conservative sampling heuristics, and an investigative dashboard layout optimized for fast triage of latency/cost/quality issues.

If you read this and want to try something, add a note in the linked jira or ping #obs-lab on Slack and we'll carve out a short run.
